description: Mazdutide is a long-acting oxyntomodulin analogue engineered as a dual agonist at the glucagon receptor (GCGR) and the GLP-1 receptor. Its reported research profile combines incretin-pathway signalling with glucagon-receptor-mediated energy expenditure, which is the rationale for studying it alongside single-target GLP-1 agonists in metabolic research models.

faq.question: What is Mazdutide?
faq.answer: Mazdutide (CAS 2259884-03-0) is a long-acting oxyntomodulin analogue and dual glucagon/GLP-1 receptor agonist used as a laboratory research peptide.

faq.question: How does it compare with Tirzepatide and Retatrutide?
faq.answer: Tirzepatide targets GIP and GLP-1 receptors; Retatrutide adds glucagon-receptor activity to a triple-agonist profile; Mazdutide is an oxyntomodulin-derived dual GLP-1/glucagon agonist. All three are research reagents — none is a medicine in this catalogue.
